scholarships.title: Poland My First Choice NAWA Programme

existing.description: Poland My First Choice NAWA is a Polish government scholarship that funds the statutory period of full-time second-cycle (master's) studies at academic higher education institutions supervised by the Minister of Science and Higher Education. Beneficiaries receive the NAWA Director's scholarship of PLN 1,800 per month, an exemption from tuition fees at public universities and a one-time travel lump sum. Applicants choose the university and field of study themselves and must apply for university admission independently of the NAWA application. The 2026 call (no 19/2026 of 30 April 2026) is closed and its results were published in August 2026.
eligibility: National of one of the countries and territories listed in the current call
Holds a qualifying previous higher education degree for second-cycle studies
Full-time second-cycle (master's) studies at a supervised academic HEI with a NAWA framework agreement
Applicants must apply to the university of their choice independently; NAWA does not intermediate admission
existing.eligibility_summary: Citizens of the countries and territories listed in the call, holding a previous higher education degree that qualifies them for second-cycle studies, admitted to or applying to full-time second-cycle studies in Polish or English at an academic university supervised by the Minister of Science and Higher Education that has a framework agreement with NAWA. NAWA does not act as an intermediary for university admission; the applicant applies to the university independently.
benefits: NAWA Director's scholarship of PLN 1,800 per month for the statutory period of second-cycle studies
Exemption from tuition fees at public universities
One-time lump sum for international travel to Poland
coverage: NAWA Director's scholarship of PLN 1,800 per month for the statutory period of second-cycle studies
Exemption from tuition fees at public universities
One-time lump sum for international travel to Poland
requirements: Choose the university and field of study independently from the offer published in the call
Apply for university admission separately from the NAWA scholarship application
Study full-time at an academic HEI supervised by the Minister of Science and Higher Education that has a framework agreement with NAWA
documents: NAWA scholarship application submitted in the NAWA online system
Scan of the university admission/acceptance decision or a model certificate from the university for undergraduate studies
Previous higher education diploma with certified translation
Recognised Polish or English language certificate from the current call's accepted list
existing.english_requirement: Studies may be undertaken in Polish or English; the call attaches separate lists of recognised Polish and English language certificates for the relevant academic year.
application_method: Online application in the NAWA tele-informational system (programs.nawa.gov.pl)
Separate application to the chosen university
existing.selection_notes: NAWA applies a formal eligibility check followed by a substantive merit assessment. For the 2026 call NAWA reported 42 applications from citizens of 21 countries and territories, of which 31 passed the formal assessment and went to substantive assessment.
existing.best_fit: Graduates from the countries listed in the current call who already have, or can obtain, admission to a full-time English- or Polish-language master's programme at a supervised Polish academic university.
existing.notes: The call explicitly does not cover fields of study offered by higher education institutions supervised by other ministries. Award numbers are small (19 beneficiaries for 2025/26).
existing.duration: The statutory period of full-time second-cycle (master's) studies at a Polish academic higher education institution
existing.application_period: Annual call published by NAWA each spring for the following academic year (call no 13/2025 for 2025/26; call no 19/2026 of 30 April 2026 for 2026/27)
existing.deadline_display: The 2026 call was published as 'no 19/2026 of 30th April 2026' with results announced by NAWA on 3 August 2026, so that cycle is closed. The submission deadline itself is stated inside the announcement PDF, which was not opened; no deadline date is asserted here. The next call is expected in spring 2027.
existing.program_type: Government scholarship for international master's students

existing.description: The UNESCO/Poland Co-Sponsored Fellowships in Engineering place 28 six-month research fellowships at the UNESCO Chair for Science, Technology and Engineering at AGH University of Science and Technology in Krakow at the disposal of UNESCO, for candidates from 57 invited developing Member States. The Polish authorities provide free tuition, a monthly allowance of PLN 1,800 or 2,200 and a one-time arrival allowance; UNESCO covers international travel, health insurance and a USD 120 pocket allowance. Applications must be endorsed and transmitted by the candidate's National Commission for UNESCO. The 2025 edition is closed.
eligibility: National of one of the invited Member States listed in Annex II
Holds a bachelor's, master's or PhD degree (certified copies in English, apostilled or legalised)
Endorsed and nominated by the National Commission for UNESCO of their country
Meets the field-specific qualifications in Annex III for the chosen project
Some projects are restricted to candidates from particular regions - check Annex III and Annex IV
existing.eligibility_summary: Nationals of the invited Member States listed in Annex II (57 states in the 2025 edition) who hold a bachelor's, master's or PhD degree and are nominated by their own National Commission for UNESCO. Because UNESCO is intergovernmental, individual applications are not accepted: the National Commission selects and transmits the application to UNESCO Paris. Specific qualifications per field of research are set in Annex III, and some fields are restricted to particular regions.
benefits: Free tuition for six months plus university facilities
Monthly allowance of PLN 1,800 (BSc) or PLN 2,200 (MSc)
One-time special allowance of PLN 1,800 (BSc) or PLN 2,200 (MSc) on arrival
International travel to and from Poland covered by UNESCO
Health insurance taken out and paid for by UNESCO
coverage: Free tuition for six months and access to university facilities
Monthly allowance of PLN 1,800 (BSc candidates) or PLN 2,200 (MSc candidates)
One-time special allowance of PLN 1,800 (BSc) or PLN 2,200 (MSc) on arrival in Poland
International travel to and from Poland by the most direct, economical route (UNESCO)
Health insurance for fellows declared medically fit (UNESCO)
requirements: Contact the National Commission for UNESCO of your own country first - UNESCO will not accept a direct application
Choose a maximum of three of the 28 proposed projects and give a priority number for each
Submit to your National Commission early enough for it to transmit to UNESCO by the official deadline
Once endorsed, submit the application by e-mail to agh.poland@unesco.org and complete the online information sheet
Pay for your own passport and visa expenses
documents: UNESCO fellowships application form, all 4 pages, completed in English in capital letters
Copy of the applicant's identity photo
Certified copies in English of bachelor's, master's or PhD degree, apostilled or authorised (legalised where apostille is not recognised)
UNESCO certificate of language knowledge, if the mother tongue is not English
Two letters of recommendation dated 2025 for the 2025 edition
Completed online information sheet once endorsed by the National Commission
existing.english_requirement: The UNESCO application form must be completed in English using capital letters; illegible documents are eliminated from evaluation and handwritten forms must be in capitals. Degree certificates must be certified copies in English.
application_method: National Commission for UNESCO of the candidate's country selects and transmits the application to UNESCO Paris by e-mail
Endorsed candidates then e-mail agh.poland@unesco.org (copy uniune25@agh.edu.pl and Fellowships.Engineering@unesco.pl) and complete an online information sheet
existing.selection_notes: Individual applications are not accepted by UNESCO; only applications endorsed by National Commissions are considered, and incomplete or late applications are discarded. The selection of fellowship recipients is made and decided by the concerned Polish authorities, taking into account gender equality and diversity.
existing.best_fit: BSc, MSc and PhD holders from the 57 invited Member States who need their National Commission for UNESCO to nominate them for a six-month engineering research stay at AGH University in Krakow.
existing.notes: There is a sibling award, the Programme of Fellowships under the Polish National Commission for UNESCO, which is a different scheme and must not be merged into this row.
existing.duration: 6 months of individual research, 1 October 2025 to 31 March 2026 in the 2025 edition
existing.application_period: Annual edition. For 2025 the National Commissions had to forward nominations by 26 May 2025 for a fellowship running 1 October 2025 to 31 March 2026.
existing.deadline_display: 2025 edition: 'National Commissions of invited Member States will select qualified candidates and transmit ... by Monday 26 May 2025, Midnight Paris time at the latest.' Individual applications are not accepted by UNESCO; only candidates endorsed by their National Commission are considered. That edition is closed and no 2026/27 deadline is published.
